Background (from the session that started this one):
AMU (PyPI name `anti-messup`, command `amu`, repo github.com/abslock128w/AMU, git remote named `github`, `gh` authenticated as abslock128w) posts one comment per pull request from a two-workflow GitHub Action (`evaluation/ci/INSTALL-NOTE.md`): it runs tests on the merge base and the head, reports flips (confirmed by rerun), change evidence (the PR's own tests failing on base), paired behaviour differences (each side records calls into changed functions in its own run; `amu/core/sidebyside.py`, `record.py`), and per-hunk evidence states that pick the first line (`amu/core/states.py`, `amu/ci/render.py`). Large suites use a nightly whole-suite recording (`amu-record.yml`, `amu/ci/record_suite.py`); suites that fit the 300 s budget run whole. Current release v0.7.0 (main at PR #99). Evaluation records: `evaluation/STATUS.md`, `evaluation/generalize/REPORT-v070.md` (47-PR set: Django 17, sympy 20, Flask 10, hand labels in `v070-47/labels.json`), `evaluation/pilot/{attrs,httpx,jinja}/REPORT.md` (15 replayed PRs each on forks abslock128w/{attrs,httpx,jinja}, live Action). v0.7.0 numbers: attrs 15/15 first lines, httpx 15/15 (untuned), jinja 13/15 with 121 false rows, Django 14/17 with 24 of 495 raise-catchers missed, sympy 18/20 with 79 of 11,240 missed, 2 false rows on the 47 set. Open PRs #100 (guards never crash), #101 (closure state in input digest), #102 (honest counts; has a merge conflict with main), #103 (mixed hunks, scripts/ excluded, grouped rows) are green on CI and not merged; #99 is merged. A fork abslock128w/requests exists with 15 PRs picked in `requests15.tsv` on branch `eval/v071-tools`, which also holds the evaluation harness scripts (replay, raise_missed.py, freeze). The 47-set local workspace is `~/Documents/ChatGPT/AMU/generalize-2026-11-02` (clones, envs, recordings; rebuild from `evaluation/*/freeze.json` if missing). The owner's standing: AMU is not production-ready until it generalizes; no per-repo tuning, fix causes; losses first; freeze the engine by script before every measurement, never edit engine code while a run is live; each fix is its own PR with a test that fails on the old code; never run an upstream suite without approval (approved: Django, sympy, Flask, Click, Werkzeug, attrs, httpx, jinja, requests); never create new public repositories or touch any upstream project; never commit keys; standing authority to merge own PRs when GitHub CI is green, tag and release, delete own branches; PyPI trusted publisher is not configured (owner task), so releases are GitHub-only. The owner is away: do not stop for questions, record blockers and continue. This checkout is a worktree on branch `docs/status`; make branches from `github/main`, never commit to `docs/status`. Local recording and site-hook tests flake under load; GitHub CI is the arbiter. Run long jobs in the background and keep the laptop usable: at most two measurement streams at a time.

Task:
Three phases. Report after each with numbers first, losses first.

Phase 1, ship v0.7.1. Rebase #102 onto main and resolve its conflict; merge #100, #101, #102, #103 when green. Release v0.7.1 on GitHub (not PyPI). Pin the forks' workflows to v0.7.1 and re-run live: attrs, httpx, jinja (existing fork PRs, re-trigger or new PRs on the existing base branches) and requests (open its 15 PRs from requests15.tsv on the existing fork). Re-run the 47 set locally on the frozen v0.7.1 engine with the raise measure. Targets: Django missed catchers 0 (fix 1 is in), jinja false rows 0, every first line that was wrong at v0.7.0 now right, no regressions. Reports: update evaluation/pilot/*/REPORT.md with before/after, write evaluation/generalize/REPORT-v071.md, evaluation/pilot/requests/REPORT.md.

Phase 2, the regression set. AMU's main signal, a flip, has never fired on a real merged PR in any set (0 flips across 107 PRs), so its true-positive rate is unmeasured. Build evaluation/regressions/: mine the git history of Django, sympy, Flask, attrs, httpx, jinja and requests for merged PRs that introduced a test failure fixed later (signals: a later commit or PR titled "fix regression", "revert", "fixes #N" where N references a bug reported after the PR merged, or a test added later that fails on the PR's head). Verify each candidate by running the later test on the PR's merge base, head, and the fix commit: it must pass, fail, pass. Target 30 confirmed regression PRs across the repos. Then replay each through AMU (local, frozen v0.7.1 engine, same budget as the Action): did AMU post a flip or a behaviour row that names the regressed function? Report: caught / missed per repo, with each miss traced to a cause (test not selected, test not in the suite at that time, flip rejected by trust layer, budget). Do not fix anything in this phase; record causes with reproductions. Write evaluation/regressions/REPORT.md with PROTOCOL.md (how candidates were mined and verified) and labels.json.

Phase 3, measurement trust. Add to evaluation/PROTOCOL.md: (a) a rubric version on every labels.json and every table (start at rubric v3 for the current rules; back-label the v0.6.0 and v0.7.0 tables with their rubric versions); (b) a blind second labeling: write evaluation/blind/ with 20 comments drawn at random from the 47 set and the live sets, with PR ids stripped, and a script that lets a separate session label them without seeing the existing labels; run it yourself in a fresh subagent that is given only the comments and the rubric, and report agreement with the existing labels per field; (c) stability: run 10 of the 47 PRs three times each on the frozen engine and report how many first lines and row counts are identical across trials. Write the numbers into evaluation/STATUS.md with a new section "How much to trust these numbers".

Final message: Phase 1 per-repo table (first line, useful, noise, false rows, missed catchers, suite share), Phase 2 caught/missed table with causes, Phase 3 agreement and stability numbers, then losses, then unfinished and why.

def nightly(clone, merge_base):
    when = D.datetime.fromtimestamp(int(git(clone, 'show', '-s', '--format=%ct', merge_base)), D.timezone.utc)
    cut = when.replace(hour=3, minute=23, second=0, microsecond=0)
    if cut > when:
        cut -= D.timedelta(days=1)
    return git(clone, 'rev-list', '-1', f'--before={cut.isoformat()}', merge_base)


def main():

    p.add_argument('--engine', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--repos', nargs='+', default=['django', 'sympy'])
    p.add_argument('--only', nargs='*', type=int)

install lines set to CMD. --main commits them to the fork's default branch (the posting workflow runs only from
there). Each base branch is <prefix>-base-<merge base[:10]> = merge base + one commit adding the workflows; each head

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

W = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
NAME, EMAIL = 'abslock128w', 'rajesh.v@vmrcloudsolutions.com'
TRAILER = 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'


def git(clone, *args, check=True):
    done = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(clone), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and done.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(f'git {" ".join(args)}: {done.stderr}')
    return done.stdout.strip()


def workflows(install, templates):
    out = {}
    for name in ('amu-pr.yml', 'amu-pr-comment.yml'):
        text = (Path(templates)/name).read_text()
        if name == 'amu-pr.yml':
            text = text.replace('install: python -m pip install -e .', 'install: ' + install)
            assert text.count('install: ' + install) == 2, 'both install lines'
        out[name] = text
    return out


def commit_on(clone, start, files, message, branch):
    work = W/'replay-work'
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(work), check=False)
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'add', '-q', '--detach', str(work), start)
    folder = work/'.github'/'workflows'
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name, text in files.items():
        (folder/name).write_text(text)
    git(work, 'add', '.github/workflows/amu-pr.yml', '.github/workflows/amu-pr-comment.yml')
    git(work, '-c', f'user.name={NAME}', '-c', f'user.email={EMAIL}', 'commit', '-qm', message, '-m', TRAILER)
    git(work, 'branch', '-f', branch, 'HEAD')
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(work))

    p.add_argument('--fork', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--list', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--install', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--prefix', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--upstream', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--main', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--open', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--release', default='v0.6.0')
    p.add_argument('--templates', default=str(W/'rel'/'ci'))
    a = p.parse_args()
    clone, files = Path(a.clone), workflows(a.install, a.templates)
    rows = [line.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for line in Path(a.list).read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    git(clone, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin')
    if a.main:
        default = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', f'repos/{a.fork}', '--jq', '{b: .default_branch}']))['b']
        git(clone, 'fetch', '-q', 'fork', default, check=False)
        start = f'fork/{default}' if git(clone, 'rev-parse', '-q', '--verify', f'fork/{default}', check=False) else f'origin/{default}'
        commit_on(clone, start, files, f'Install the AMU pull request workflows (AMU {a.release}) for a replay pilot on this fork',
                  'replay-main')
        git(clone, 'push', '-q', 'fork', f'replay-main:refs/heads/{default}')
    refs = []
    for number, base, head, *_ in rows:
        branch = f'{a.prefix}-base-{base[:10]}'
        commit_on(clone, base, files, f'Add the AMU pull request workflows (AMU {a.release}) at merge base {base[:10]}', branch)

    git(clone, 'push', '-q', 'fork', *sorted(set(refs)))

                    f'upstream merge base {base[:10]} plus one commit adding the AMU workflows. Head: the pull request\'s own '
                    'commits. Not for merging.')
            made = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', f'repos/{a.fork}/pulls', '-f', f'title=Replay {number} ({a.release}): {title.replace("#", "")}',

"""Collect a fork pilot's live results: per pull request the AMU job time, open-to-comment time, the comment, and the
artifact (report.json, meta.json, patch.diff). Usage: python collect.py --fork owner/name --opened FILE --out DIR
FILE rows: fork PR number, upstream number, created_at (as printed by replay.py)."""
import argparse
import datetime as D
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


def api(path):
    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', path]))


def when(text):
    return D.datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace('Z', '+00:00'))


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--fork', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--opened', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    a = p.parse_args()
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = []
    for line in Path(a.opened).read_text().splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit():
            continue
        first, second, created = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), parts[2]
        rows.append((min(first, second), max(first, second), created))  # the fork's numbers are the small ones
    runs = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/actions/runs?per_page=100&event=pull_request')['workflow_runs']
    comments = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        got = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/issues/comments?per_page=100&page={page}')
        comments += got
        if len(got) < 100:
            break
        page += 1
    table = []
    for fork_pr, upstream, created in rows:
        pr = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/pulls/{fork_pr}')
        mine = [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'AMU pull request' and r['head_sha'] == pr['head']['sha']
                and any(x['number'] == fork_pr for x in r.get('pull_requests') or [])] or \
               [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'AMU pull request' and r['head_sha'] == pr['head']['sha'] and r['created_at'] >= created]
        run = sorted(mine, key=lambda r: r['created_at'])[-1] if mine else None
        jobs = api(f"repos/{a.fork}/actions/runs/{run['id']}/jobs")['jobs'] if run else []
        amu = next((j for j in jobs if j['name'] == 'amu' and j.get('completed_at')), None)
        posted = [c for c in comments if c['issue_url'].endswith(f'/issues/{fork_pr}')]
        folder = out/str(upstream)
        folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        if run:
            subprocess.run(['gh', 'run', 'download', '-R', a.fork, str(run['id']), '-n', 'amu-report', '-D', str(folder)],
                           capture_output=True)
        body = posted[-1]['body'] if posted else ''
        (folder/'comment.md').write_text(body)
        row = dict(upstream=upstream, fork_pr=fork_pr, run=run['id'] if run else None,
                   amu_job_s=(when(amu['completed_at']) - when(amu['started_at'])).seconds if amu else None,
                   queue_s=(when(amu['started_at']) - when(created)).seconds if amu else None,
                   opened_to_comment_s=(when(posted[-1]['created_at']) - when(created)).seconds if posted else None,
                   posted=bool(posted), first=body.splitlines()[0] if body else None)
        table.append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
    (out/'live.json').write_text(json.dumps(table, indent=1))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# AMU status (v0.5.1, 2026-11-02)

Building has stopped at v0.5.1. This page says what AMU does, how it scored on the last test set, what it still gets wrong, and what real use would have to show before the engine changes again. To install it, see [ci/INSTALL-NOTE.md](ci/INSTALL-NOTE.md).

## What AMU does on a pull request

Two workflow files run on every push to a pull request, and AMU edits one comment each time. It never blocks a merge.

1. **Flips.** It runs the tests the diff reaches on the merge base and on the head, up to 300 s of test time per side. A test that passes on the base and fails on the head is a flip. Each flip is rerun on the base before it counts, and again in a fresh job when the optional verify job is installed. Tests the pull request itself edited are listed apart, not counted.
2. **Change evidence.** The pull request's own new or edited tests are run on the base. One that fails there, passes on the head, and fails again alone in a fresh process shows the change does what it checks. A test that fails only because the code it calls is new is filed as "new test for new code".
3. **Behaviour differences.** For each changed function the tests call, side-by-side runs the code before and after the change on copies of the same captured arguments. It lists only results that differ and that both versions repeat.
4. **First line.** One of:
   - "N flips"
   - "0 flips, some of them on the changed code"
   - "no test ran the changed code in …"
   - "adds new code only"
   - "refactor only" (no tests run)
   - "docstring or comment changes only"
   - "no flip count", with the reason

   Anything not run or not seen is listed under Gaps.

## Numbers on the 47-pull-request set

The set is 17 Django, 20 sympy and 10 Flask pull requests merged after the earlier evaluation windows (`performance-v042/freeze.json`). Each comment was hand-labelled (`performance-fixes/labels.json`).

| | v0.4.2 | v0.5.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| First line correct | 37 of 47 | 42 of 47 |
| Adds something a reviewer would want | 15 | 19 |
| Adds nothing (correct, but no more than green CI says) | 25 | 26 |
| Adds noise | 7 | 2 |
| Behaviour-difference rows: false | 102 of 125 | 1 of 34 |
| Counted flips | 0 | 0 |

Every "adds something" case is change evidence: the pull request's own test fails on the base and passes on the head, which project CI never shows, or a behaviour row the description does not mention. No pull request in the set broke an existing test, so the flip count, AMU's main signal, was never tested here. The earlier 100-PR retrospective found 0 false flips among 30 counted (`retrospective/REPORT.md`).

## The five pull requests where the first line is still wrong

| PR | Cause |
|---|---|
| Django #21887 | A class attribute turned into a property is not a side-by-side target, so whether a test reached it is unknown (engine). The code only runs on MySQL with a GIS backend, which AMU cannot provide. |
| Django #22158 | A new class plus a registry entry is not a side-by-side target (engine). The code only runs on Python 3.15, which AMU cannot know. |
| Django #22187 | A change to module-level data (`LANG_INFO`) has no measure of whether any test read it (engine). The first line is true but does not say the change is data (judgment). |
| sympy #30809 | `__slots__ = ()` on a mixin is a class attribute with no reach measure, and the PR's own test is filed as "new test for new code" because its error message names `__slots__` (engine). |
| sympy #29693 | "Adds new code only" treats a new method as unused, but this one is found by name lookup and changes `latex()` output (engine, judgment on which new methods count as reachable). |

Other known limits:
- Flask #5812 keeps one false behaviour row (`make_default_options_response`).
- Django `subTest` failures are not parsed (Django #22176, noise).

## What would justify the next engine change

After a month on at least one real repository with `counters: 'true'` (per-push counts and SHAs only, kept in the comment), a maintainer would need to see:

1. **Flips that are real.** At least 10 posted flips, with no more than 1 in 10 not caused by the change. The fresh-job rerun and the maintainer's own reading decide which are real.
2. **Flips acted on.** At least 3 pull requests where a flip AMU named was fixed by a later push before merge, visible in the counters as a flip that disappears with no edit to that test.
3. **Comments read.** The maintainer can name pull requests where the change evidence or a behaviour row changed what they reviewed or asked for. Without that, the 19 "adds something" labels above are only this evaluation's judgment.
4. **The misses matter there.** A class of the five misses above shows up in at least 3 of their pull requests before it is worth an engine change.

If flips stay at zero for the month, the flip path is still unmeasured. The question then is whether change evidence alone earns the job time: a median of 2 to 5 minutes on Django and sympy, and under 20 s on Flask.

## Known limit: coverage that depends on test order

Some suites share state across tests, sympy's cache for one. Whether a test reaches a line then depends on which tests
ran before it, and a suite recording made in one order can miss a test that reaches the changed code when it runs in
another. On the 47 set at v0.7.0 this hid 77 of 3,027 tests that would catch a raise on sympy 30815. Recorded on their

"""Draw the blind second-labeling set: 20 comments at random from the v0.7.0 labels (the 47 set and the attrs, httpx
and jinja live pilots), with pull request ids stripped.

Usage: python make.py --patches DIR [--seed 20261109] [--n 20]
DIR holds the runs' patches: DIR/out-e43bcd672/<repo>/<n>/patch.diff (47 set) and DIR/live-<repo>[-v070]/<n>/patch.diff.
Writes items/NN/{comment.md, patch.diff} and key.json (item -> source and the existing labels, rubric v3).
A labeler reads RUBRIC.md and items/ only; key.json is read by score.py alone.
"""
import argparse
import json
import random
import re
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
EVAL = HERE.parent
SOURCES = [  # set, labels file, comments folder, patch folder under --patches
    ('47', 'generalize/v070-47/labels.json', 'generalize/v070-47/comments/{repo}/{n}.md', 'out-e43bcd672/{repo}/{n}'),
    ('attrs', 'pilot/attrs/v070/labels.json', 'pilot/attrs/v070/comments/{n}.md', 'live-attrs-v070/{n}'),
    ('httpx', 'pilot/httpx/v070/labels.json', 'pilot/httpx/v070/comments/{n}.md', 'live-httpx-v070/{n}'),
    ('jinja', 'pilot/jinja/labels.json', 'pilot/jinja/comments/{n}.md', 'live-jinja/{n}'),
]
FIELDS = ('first_line_correct', 'adds', 'false_rows', 'real_rows')


def labels_of(entry):
    """The four compared fields, under one name each (the 47 set says false/real, the pilots false_rows/real_rows)."""
    return dict(first_line_correct=entry['first_line_correct'], adds=entry['adds'],
                false_rows=entry.get('false_rows', entry.get('false', 0)) or 0,
                real_rows=entry.get('real_rows', entry.get('real', 0)) or 0)


def strip(text, number, shas):
    """Remove what names the pull request: its number and every commit id."""
    text = re.sub(r'\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b', '<sha>', text)
    for sha in shas:
        text = text.replace(sha, '<sha>')
    return re.sub(rf'(?<![\w.:/-]){number}(?![\w.])', '<pr>', text)


def pool(patches):
    out = []
    for name, labels, comment, patch in SOURCES:
        for key, entry in json.loads((EVAL/labels).read_text()).items():
            repo, n = (key.split('#') if '#' in key else (name, key))
            fields = dict(repo=repo, n=n)
            c, p = EVAL/comment.format(**fields), Path(patches)/patch.format(**fields)/'patch.diff'
            if c.exists() and p.exists():
                out.append(dict(set=name, repo=repo, number=int(n), comment=c, patch=p, labels=labels_of(entry)))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: (x['set'], x['repo'], x['number']))


def main():
    a = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    a.add_argument('--patches', required=True)
    a.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=20261109)
    a.add_argument('--n', type=int, default=20)
    args = a.parse_args()
    everything = pool(args.patches)
    drawn = random.Random(args.seed).sample(everything, args.n)
    key = dict(seed=args.seed, pool=len(everything), rubric='v3', items={})
    for i, item in enumerate(drawn, 1):
        folder = HERE/'items'/f'{i:02d}'
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        meta = json.loads((item['patch'].parent/'meta.json').read_text()) if (item['patch'].parent/'meta.json').exists() else {}
        shas = [v for v in meta.values() if isinstance(v, str) and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{40}', v)]
        (folder/'comment.md').write_text(strip(item['comment'].read_text(), item['number'], shas))
        (folder/'patch.diff').write_text(strip(item['patch'].read_text(), item['number'], shas))

"""Agreement between a blind labeler's answers and the existing labels (key.json), per field.

Usage: python score.py [--labeler blind]
Rows: exact agreement for first_line_correct and adds (with Cohen's kappa), and for the row counts both exact
agreement and agreement on whether any false (or real) row exists. Writes agreement-<labeler>.json.
"""
import argparse
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def kappa(pairs):
    n = len(pairs)
    if not n:
        return None
    seen = sum(a == b for a, b in pairs) / n
    left, right = Counter(a for a, _ in pairs), Counter(b for _, b in pairs)
    chance = sum(left[k] * right[k] for k in set(left) | set(right)) / (n * n)
    return None if chance == 1 else round((seen - chance) / (1 - chance), 2)


def main():
    a = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    a.add_argument('--labeler', default='blind')
    args = a.parse_args()
    key = json.loads((HERE/'key.json').read_text())
    answers = json.loads((HERE/f'answers-{args.labeler}.json').read_text())
    common = sorted(set(key['items']) & set(answers))
    out = dict(labeler=args.labeler, rubric=key['rubric'], items=len(common), fields={}, disagreements=[])
    tests = dict(first_line_correct=lambda v: v, adds=lambda v: v, false_rows=lambda v: v, real_rows=lambda v: v,
                 any_false_row=lambda v: v > 0, any_real_row=lambda v: v > 0)
    for field, f in tests.items():
        source = field.replace('any_false_row', 'false_rows').replace('any_real_row', 'real_rows')
        pairs = [(f(key['items'][i]['labels'][source]), f(answers[i][source])) for i in common]
        out['fields'][field] = dict(agree=sum(x == y for x, y in pairs), of=len(pairs),
                                    kappa=kappa(pairs) if field in ('first_line_correct', 'adds', 'any_false_row') else None)
    for i in common:
        diff = {k: dict(existing=key['items'][i]['labels'][k], blind=answers[i][k])
                for k in ('first_line_correct', 'adds', 'false_rows', 'real_rows')
                if key['items'][i]['labels'][k] != answers[i][k]}
        if diff:
            item = key['items'][i]
            out['disagreements'].append(dict(item=i, source=f"{item['set']}:{item['repo']}#{item['number']}", fields=diff,
                                             note=answers[i].get('note', '')))
    (HERE/f'agreement-{args.labeler}.json').write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1) + '\n')
    for field, r in out['fields'].items():
        print(f"{field}: {r['agree']} of {r['of']}" + (f", kappa {r['kappa']}" if r['kappa'] is not None else ''))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Labeling rubric v3, for the blind second labeling

This is rubric v3 from `evaluation/PROTOCOL.md` without its worked examples (they name pull requests from the pool).
For each item you have the AMU comment (`comment.md`) and the pull request's diff (`patch.diff`). Commit ids are
replaced by `<sha>` and the pull request number by `<pr>`. Label four fields.

## AMU in one paragraph

AMU runs the tests a diff reaches on the merge base and on the head. A **flip** is a test that passes on the base and
fails on the head. **Change evidence**: the pull request's own new or edited tests that fail on the base and pass on
the head. **Behaviour differences**: calls into changed functions, captured with the same input on both sides, whose
results differ. Each changed hunk gets a state (ran on both sides, ran only in the PR's own tests, ran in no test, not
executable here, at import, not recorded...). The **first line** (bold, first line of the comment) summarises it.

## 1. first_line_correct: right or wrong

Judge every clause of the first line, not only its category. It is right only when every clause is true of this pull
request and none says something a reader would take to be false. It is wrong when any of these holds:

1. No report (the line says AMU exited or crashed with no report).
2. A category header that does not fit the whole diff: "docstring or comment changes only", "type annotations only",
   "adds new code only" are right only when every changed production line is of that kind ("adds new code only" is
   wrong if the new code changes existing behaviour, e.g. found by name dispatch).
3. "ran all N tests" when a large part of the suite gave no outcome (hundreds of tests). A handful unrunnable is fine.
4. "every changed hunk ran on both sides, in up to N tests" when some code hunk did not run on both sides. A hunk
   counts as run when any line in it ran.
5. "(at import)" is right for lines that run when the module loads (version strings, `__all__`, module data,
   `__slots__`, imports). It is wrong when a hunk is a function body that ran only in the pull request's own tests
   (the line should then say so), or code under a def that cannot run here.
6. "in up to N tests" must count tests that ran the changed lines, not only the def line.
7. "ran only in the pull request's own tests: path:line" is wrong if another test reaches that hunk.
8. "N of M changed hunks ran in no test: ..." is wrong when a named hunk ran in some test; when the test run was cut off
   before every candidate ran (a cut run can only say "not recorded"); or when a named hunk is a docstring or comment
   edit inside code that did run. It stays right when the named hunks are true but of low value (type-check example
   files, annotations on uncalled code, overload stubs), and ordering is not judged.
9. "not executable on <Python/platform> here (needs <guard>)" is right when the named line cannot run in this job. It is
   wrong when the line itself runs and only one operand of an expression on it is gated. A repeated phrase that does not
   change the claim is not wrong.
10. "N tests of the pull request's own fail on the merge base and pass on the head" must be true for each test counted.
11. "N behaviour differences on the same input" makes the line wrong when the rows it announces are false. Real rows,
   however many, keep it right.

Where a fact can't be checked from the diff and comment (did this test run that line?), judge from what the comment
reports and the diff shows; do not assume a defect you can't see.

## 2. adds: something, nothing or noise

"Something" is something a reviewer cannot read from the diff and description.

- **something**: at least one of: a bug fix's own test failing on the merge base and passing on the head (the test
  reproduces the bug, which CI never shows); a real behaviour row the description does not make obvious; a hunk no
  test reaches that the diff does not show as unreached; a hunk named as not executable on this job's Python or
  platform when that is not obvious from the diff.
- **nothing**: the comment is right (or wrong only by omission) and says no more than the diff, description or green
  CI: own tests failing on the base only for want of a new feature, or whose base failure is evident from the diff;
  real, intended rows the description or diff already states; platform-gated code a reviewer knows doesn't run here;
  moves, version bumps, docstring-only, annotation-only changes. A wrong first line does not by itself make it noise.
- **noise**: the comment asserts something false a reviewer would act on, or buries the true part: false behaviour
  rows announced; "evidence" tests that fail only because the code is new; a wrong count of tests run.

## 3. false_rows and real_rows (integers; 0 when the comment lists no behaviour rows)

Count the rows the comment lists under behaviour differences (a grouped line "K calls show this change" counts K).
- **real**: the difference follows from what the diff changes in that function (its result, type, value or message).
- **false**: the difference comes from how the two sides were run, not from the change (values derived from each
  side's tree such as version strings or paths, lazily filled caches, closure state, objects built by old code).
- A row whose before and after previews look equal and that you can't trace: false, unless the diff changes what that
  function returns, then real.
real_rows + false_rows = the number of rows listed.

"""Verify regression candidates: the later test must pass on the culprit PR's merge base, fail on its head, and pass on
the fix commit. The test files the fix commit adds or changes are laid over each tree (a test that does not exist yet
at base or head is taken from the fix).

Usage: python verify.py --candidates candidates.json --out verified.jsonl [--only ID ...] [--timeout 600]
Each output row: id, repo, outcomes {base, head, fix} as pass/fail/error/missing, verdict confirmed/rejected/unrunnable,
and the tail of each run's output. Rows already in --out are skipped.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

W = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CLONES = dict(django=W/'repos'/'django', sympy=W/'repos'/'sympy', flask=W/'repos'/'flask', attrs=W/'attrs',
              httpx=W/'httpx', jinja=W/'jinja', requests=W/'requests')
PYTHONS = dict(django=W/'env'/'django', sympy=W/'env'/'sympy', flask=W/'env'/'flask', attrs=W/'attrsvenv',
               httpx=W/'httpxvenv', jinja=W/'jinjavenv', requests=W/'requestsvenv')


def git(repo, *args, check=False):
    done = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and done.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(done.stderr)
    return done.stdout.strip()


def cid(c):
    return f"{c['repo']}:{(c.get('culprit_pr') or c['culprit_sha'][:10])}:{c['fix_sha'][:10]}"


def test_files(clone, fix):
    """Test files the fix commit adds or modifies."""
    names = git(clone, 'diff-tree', '--no-commit-id', '--name-status', '-r', f'{fix}^', fix).splitlines()
    return [line.split('\t')[-1] for line in names if line[:1] in 'AM' and re.search(r'(^|/)tests?(/|_)|_test\.py$|/test_', line)]


def command(repo, tree, python, tests):
    if repo == 'django':
        labels = [t.replace('tests/', '', 1) if t.startswith('tests/') else t for t in tests]
        return [str(python), 'tests/runtests.py', '--parallel', '1', '--noinput', *labels]
    return [str(python), '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', '-o', 'addopts=', *tests]


def outcome(repo, done):
    text = done.stdout + done.stderr
    if done.returncode == 0:
        return 'pass'
    if re.search(r'(ERROR: (file or directory )?not found|no tests ran|ImportError|ModuleNotFoundError|SyntaxError|'
                 r'errors? during collection|AttributeError: module .* has no attribute)', text) and not re.search(
                 r'\bFAILED\b|^FAIL:', text, re.M):
        return 'error'
    return 'fail'


def run_at(c, label, commit, files, timeout):
    clone, python = CLONES[c['repo']], PYTHONS[c['repo']]/'bin'/'python'
    tree = W/'regwork'/'verify'/label
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(tree))
    shutil.rmtree(tree, ignore_errors=True)
    tree.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', '-q', str(tree), commit, check=True)
    for f in files:  # the fix's version of each test file
        (tree/f).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tree/f).write_bytes(subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(clone), 'show', f"{c['fix_sha']}:{f}"], capture_output=True).stdout)
    env = dict({k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith('ANTHROPIC_')},
               PYTHONPATH=os.pathsep.join([str(tree/'src'), str(tree)]), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1')
    cwd = tree/'tests' if c['repo'] == 'django' else tree
    cmd = command(c['repo'], tree, python, c['tests'])
    if c['repo'] == 'django':
        cmd[1] = 'runtests.py'
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=timeout)
        result = outcome(c['repo'], done), (done.stdout + done.stderr)[-1500:]
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        result = 'error', 'timeout'
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(tree))
    return result


def main():
    a = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    a.add_argument('--candidates', required=True)
    a.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    a.add_argument('--only', nargs='*')
    a.add_argument('--timeout', type=int, default=600)
    args = a.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    done = {json.loads(line)['id'] for line in out.read_text().splitlines()} if out.exists() else set()
    for c in json.loads(Path(args.candidates).read_text()):
        key = cid(c)
        if key in done or (args.only and key not in args.only) or not c.get('tests'):
            continue
        clone = CLONES[c['repo']]
        for sha in (c['base'], c['head'], c['fix_sha']):
            if git(clone, 'cat-file', '-t', sha) != 'commit':
                git(clone, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin', sha)
        files = test_files(clone, c['fix_sha'])
        outcomes, tails = {}, {}
        for side, commit in (('base', c['base']), ('head', c['head']), ('fix', c['fix_sha'])):
            outcomes[side], tails[side] = run_at(c, f"{c['repo']}-{side}", commit, files, args.timeout)
        if outcomes == dict(base='pass', head='fail', fix='pass'):
            verdict = 'confirmed'
        elif 'error' in (outcomes['head'], outcomes['fix'], outcomes['base']):
            verdict = 'unrunnable'
        else:
            verdict = 'rejected'
        row = dict(id=key, repo=c['repo'], culprit_pr=c.get('culprit_pr'), base=c['base'], head=c['head'], fix=c['fix_sha'],
                   tests=c['tests'], overlaid=files, outcomes=outcomes, verdict=verdict, tails=tails)
        with out.open('a') as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(row) + '\n')
        print(json.dumps(dict(id=key, outcomes=outcomes, verdict=verdict)), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
